purpose: The time as a bar sign: HH:MM in continuous bent pink tube, dim blacked-out return tubes and mounting standoffs, a colon that breathes once a second and one stroke that stutters once a minute. It refuses seven segments and any second colour.

accent.where: the whole sign, one pink tube; brightness carries the hierarchy

night.recipe: The lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes (the Vinyl precedent); the mat around it, visible on the square device, flips with --face-bg, and night dimming comes from the kiosk brightness. For a dark room the glow option pulls the halo in.

options.intent: full is the neon as designed; soft keeps the tubes and their white cores but pulls the halo in, the setting for a clock by the bed.

antiPatterns.rule: Never paint the neon or the stage with --face-ink or --face-bg
antiPatterns.why: the lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes, like the Vinyl record; the day ink is black and would vanish on it, so only the mat outside the disc reads --face-bg

antiPatterns.rule: Never draw the still parts live every frame
antiPatterns.why: nine glow passes per stroke made the drafts cost 17 to 20 ms a frame at 1080; anything that changes at most once a minute goes through N.layer in src/apps/clock/neon/faces/sign.ts or the Pi drops frames

antiPatterns.rule: Do not redraw the lettering as seven segments
antiPatterns.why: the face is a bent-tube sign; segment digits would make it a generic LED clock and lose the one thing it is

specless: Drawn on a canvas by src/apps/clock/neon/faces/sign.ts in the shared 1000-unit space. Bent-tube numerals, return tubes and standoffs have no place in the spec vocabulary of solid hands and two tick rings, so the numbers live in the draw module.
